newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's govt unveils steps to boost stock market.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's govt unveils steps to boost stock market.

text.p: The Finance and Economy Ministry said on Monday it would liberalise interest rates on customer deposits at brokerage firms for stock investment to within five percent per year against a fixed three percent at present.
The ministry said in a statement the step was part of a plan to help boost the stock market, which has been languishing due to a lack of liquidity.
Under the plan, the ministry will also liberalise maturity and interest rates on loans that brokerage firms extend to their customers for stock margin trading.
Interest rates on such loans are currently set at 11.0 percent per year and the maturity at three months, a statement from the ministry said.
The statement also said the ministry would ease money supply policies to bring down interest rates on the money market, but it did not give details.
The ministry plans to draw up guidelines to boost stock buying by pension funds, it said, but also without elaborating.
